resolved_by: Supreme Court's decision in Pulsifer v. United States, 601 U.S. 124 (2024), which adopted the disjunctive reading of 18 U.S.C. § 3553(f)(1)
issue: Under the safety valve in 18 U.S.C. § 3553(f)(1), should the word 'and' linking the criminal-history disqualifiers be read conjunctively (defendant ineligible only if he has all three types of prior offenses) or disjunctively (ineligible if he has any one)?

sides.position: Disjunctive reading: a defendant is safety-valve ineligible if he has any one of the three listed prior offenses (adopted in Pulsifer and followed by this court)
cases: United States v. Pulsifer, 39 F.4th 1018 (8th Cir. 2022)
United States v. Palomares, 52 F.4th 640 (5th Cir. 2022)
United States v. Haynes, 55 F.4th 1075 (6th Cir. 2022)
United States v. Pace, 48 F.4th 741 (7th Cir. 2022)
United States v. Engstrom, No. 24-1878 (9th Cir. 2026)

sides.position: Conjunctive reading: a defendant is safety-valve ineligible only if he has all three listed prior offenses (former Ninth Circuit position, since abrogated)
cases: United States v. Lopez, 58 F.4th 1108 (9th Cir.)

this_court: Adopts the disjunctive reading, following Pulsifer; the Ninth Circuit's contrary Lopez position is abrogated
quote: The Supreme Court decided Pulsifer in March 2024, shortly after Engstrom's resentencing hearing, to resolve a long-standing circuit split interpreting § 3553(f)(1).
cite: United States v. Engstrom, No. 24-1878 (9th Cir. 2026)
